A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PHANTOMCIRCUIT work. Their complete main text, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching retained experiments across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original training-dynamics experiments, attention/circuit analyses and circuit-based recovery cases in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds head-ablation experiments, natural-language circuit-size analyses and an exploratory multi-hop example.

M1.justification: The recovery procedure gains a coarse edge-count scan before golden-section search, variance-weighted R-PMI for identifying Xsub, and original-rank weighting for identifying Ysub (Sections 3.2.4 and B.1–B.2). These refine the existing pipeline; circuit construction and training objectives remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the synthetic-token and fabricated-natural-language datasets. v3 Appendix E additionally evaluates natural factual prompts about a North Korean politician/singer and reports a preliminary multi-hop/negation probe. These are limited scenario extensions, rather than a broad new benchmark.

E2.justification: The full-model versus optimized-circuit comparison remains. No new competing detection or mitigation method is evaluated. GPT-2-medium and OLMo are additional models being analyzed; the head-removal variants are ablations.

E3.justification: The existing training settings and 500-dominant/500-subordinate evaluation sampling remain. New protocols remove the top 10%, 20% and 50% of attention heads, sweep circuit edge counts on fixed pretrained-model prompts, and test additional GPT-2-medium and OLMo model settings.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends the mechanistic validation beyond v1's observational analyses and recovery cases. Section 4.3 adds direct head-removal interventions testing circuit faithfulness; Appendix E adds edge-count sensitivity analyses on natural prompts and an exploratory multi-hop case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed/run counts, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The variance introduced in v3 Appendix B.2 is an algorithmic token weight, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds a substantial mechanistic-validation result set while retaining the main dynamics plots and four recovery cases. Table 1 reports M degradation of 1.03/1.43/1.67 for GPT-2-medium and 0.92/1.30/1.42 for Pythia-410m at 10%/20%/50% ablation. Figure 8 adds nonmonotonic edge-count/performance curves, and Appendix E adds OLMo outputs.

T1.justification: v3 adds a formal characterization of overshadowed circuits using the sign of M and an edge-score threshold, plus weighted R-PMI and rank-elevation definitions. Existing AO, RO and attribution formulas remain; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about training dynamics, attention-based mechanisms and circuit optimization as a promising mitigation strategy. The revised abstract wording and additional evidence do not materially redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new ablations as faithfulness evidence and explains the multimodal edge-count relationship. Its limitations explicitly address architecture and noisy-data generalization and code-generation applicability. It removes v1's specific discussion of instance-specific recovery, identification precision and a comprehensive mitigation evaluation.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a repository link in the abstract, whereas v1 only promises code upon acceptance; the old promise remains in v3's footnote. Appendices B.1–B.2 also document the search and weighting procedures more explicitly. The supplied PDFs do not establish the repository's actual contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hakimi and Zucchet to the circuit-evolution discussion and Hanna and Marks to the attribution/faithfulness rationale. It identifies the construction approach more specifically as EAP-IG with Hanna's citation. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 locally revises the abstract and methodology explanations, rewrites limitations, and adds Section 4.3, Appendix E, acknowledgments and contact information. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the explanatory Figure 2, ablation Table 1 and edge-count Figure 8. Figure 1 changes its illustrative example, and the circuit-analysis graphic adjusts its callout routing. Existing plots and appendix tables are largely retained and renumbered within the same layout.

improvement.justification: The head interventions strengthen support for the attention mechanism, while the recovery descriptions and explicit generalization limits improve clarity. These gains are limited by the case-based natural-language evidence and lack of broad recovery validation. Removing v1's specific caution about instance-level recovery is a modest tradeoff, but the added evidence and explanations provide a net improvement.
